reviewer: Codex qualitative inspection of top terms and three stored source excerpts per topic
selection_bias: Top-weight examples only; not random samples. No coherence or topic accuracy percentage claimed.

topics.note: Biology examples agree with species/animals/plants; chemical/water terms broaden the cluster.
God and Satan agree with religion terms, but Principle of relativity is a strong counterexample.
Diabetes, gender identity and violet have no narrow shared theme; generic words and RGB tables dominate.
All three high-weight articles are calendar days, despite occupation-based top words; list structure drives the cluster.
Number, IP address and Game Boy line support a broad computing/numbers theme, not a single narrow subject.
Top terms emphasize movies but all three exemplars are sports teams; awards/won vocabulary merges domains.
Tokyo, Great Britain and Rhine River agree with city/country/island/river terms.
Two musicians and a deaf-education pioneer support an American biographical theme, not a pure music topic.
Nazism, Richard Nixon and Lyndon B. Johnson agree with government/president/war terms.
Three rock bands support music terms, but language/words terms indicate another merged domain.
